results.command: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1 claude -p 'Use the Agent tool to start a subagent that uses the Agent tool to start one that replies nested-ok...' --permission-mode auto (run 3 times); then =3 with three levels
results.excerpt: Budgets measured and consistent with logs: SessionStart no-timeout hook ran full 70s (end line 10:14:54.979 from start 10:13:44.657), PreToolUse 20s, timeout:5 killed after 4 ticks, mod hook budget {ms:10000} with 15s loop not aborted. =3: reproduced nested-3-ok. But the report's depth=1 claim ('a subagent has no Agent tool') did NOT reproduce: all 3 reruns with =1 returned nested-ok from the second level. The recorded =1 evidence is a single run (run 3) whose subagent was haiku in a different setup; the depth finding is unreliable as written.

Working-tree case: commit f993518 'probe: self-edit while loaded' changing plugins/platform-probe/hooks/register.ts, no refusal. Released-copy case: commit 6d56840 in ccp_xstate_scratch changes plugins/effect-harness/hooks/register.ts (Claude-Session trailer matches thread); effect-harness appears in the session's claude.json, so it was installed. Weak spot: no fixture inside ccp_xstate records that the released copy was loaded at that moment.

send_later wake (no person message; 'user last wrote 7m ago' reminder only) with model_merge mcp__github__merge_pull_request on ccp_xstate_scratch#1 -> merged true sha e5129939. Allowed, but rules_in_force: none. The Expect line says 'under a pre-placed rule'; the condition was different, so the line as written is not answered. (If the person accepts 'allowed with no rule' as sufficient, this is MET in substance.)
